goal: Surface the Refusal Log: one closed refusal vocabulary over the reasons RepWorth already records, one tenant-scoped owner-safe read, and one Restraint tab on /dashboard/analytics that states what we did not do and why.
non_goals: No MCP server and no LangGraph — both were cut on 2026-08-29.
No migration. Migration 116 stays unused; every reason is already persisted with account_id.
No RLS change on flagged_responses. No policy is added to it.
No new capture layer. This feature records no new refusal and changes no gate.

judge_verdicts is OUT OF SCOPE. The judge runs on already-posted replies (judge-policy.ts:9, judge-store.ts:115, judge/context.ts:65), so a verdict is a post-publication observation, not something RepWorth chose not to do. Counting it would be false and would double-count the autonomy suspension it triggers.

The per-review auto-approval block reason is UNAVAILABLE. AutoApprovalBlockReason (22 members, worker/jobs/response-generation/auto-approval.ts:37) reaches only a logger.log call at persist.ts:570-576. The Refusal Log therefore reports that a draft was held for the owner, never why. Closing this needs a capture change and is out of scope.
No write action anywhere on the tab. Links only.
No change to /dashboard/requests, which already renders the six solicitation withhold reasons.
velocity_banked is excluded — BatchReport.tsx:27 already rules it volume shaping, not a refusal.
Owner acts are excluded: owner_veto, owner_halt, owner_excluded, owner_withdrawn.
Delivery failures are excluded: send_failed, send_exhausted, batch_expired, send_window_elapsed.
superseded and send_indeterminate are excluded — neither is a refusal.

S6 reads the solicitation_outreach WITHHELD arm only. The cancelled arm is out of scope entirely, including its admin_halt and platform_halt copies — latchHalt writes the batch halt reason through to every cancelled row, so counting them would report one batch halt once through S7 and again per outreach row.
No raw text from flagged_responses.reason reaches any API response or the browser.
user_visible_behavior: A Restraint tab appears on /dashboard/analytics and routes to /dashboard/analytics/restraint.
The tab states the total refusal count for the selected window and breaks it down by Refusal category.
The stated total equals the sum of the category counts.
Each category lists dated entries, newest first, each carrying one owner sentence.
A held-draft entry names the review it belongs to and links to it. It shows no draft text, no review text and no moderation reason.
A no-permission entry links to the contacts list.
wrong_moment, below_our_bar and missing_information entries carry no link.
The 7d/30d/90d/12w window control works on this tab exactly as on the other analytics views.
The tab follows the active location scope: account-wide when aggregate, one location when a location is selected.
An account-wide refusal, such as an autonomy suspension, appears in every location scope because it applies to every location.
A window with no refusals reads as a plain statement, not as an error or an empty grid.
An account without full subscription access sees the existing SubscriptionUnavailableCard branch.
invariants: Tenant isolation (#8): every UNION arm filters account_id, and additionally business_id in location scope for every business-keyed source. Because the arms share one statement, a structural assertion over the combined SQL cannot prove per-arm scoping — every arm carries its own behavioural foreign-account or foreign-location negative-row test.

Every join is scoped on both sides. flagged_responses (051:15) and approval_audit_log carry independent FKs, not tenant-composite keys, so a scoped root row can still reach a foreign review or response through an unscoped join.
flagged_responses keeps deny-all RLS. The read reaches it only through the server postgres role, scoped in the application layer.
No value read from flagged_responses.reason is selected by the query or placed in a returned object.
Domain modules take sql as an explicit parameter (#15). Only the route file imports @/lib/db/server.
The route orchestrates only (#12): resolve scope, call getRefusalLog once, return.
One authoritative vocabulary file. No refusal string literal appears at any call site.
Every source code maps explicitly to a RefusalCategory or to null. null is the decision 'not a refusal', never an omission.

Every source enum maps in under `satisfies Record<SourceEnum, RefusalCategory | null>`, so adding a member to WithholdReason, AutoPolicyDowngradeReason, AutonomySuspensionTrigger or the batch halt list fails the build until it is mapped.
The solicitation_outreach withheld vocabulary is authoritative only in the migration 111 CHECK, so its map is guarded by a test against that CHECK rather than by the type system.
Refusal category order is a closed precedence list, following the WITHHOLD_REASONS model.
edge_cases: An account with zero refusals in the window renders the empty statement.
A location with zero location-keyed refusals inside an account that has some renders only the account-keyed ones.
A flagged response whose review row is gone: the entry is dropped by the join, not rendered as a dangling link.
A suspension that was later lifted still appears, because the source is account_audit_log and not auto_approval_policies — unsuspend clears suspended_at and suspended_reason (suspension.ts:352-354).
One response downgraded twice produces two approval_audit_log rows and two dated entries.
An entry timestamped exactly at the window start is included (>=), matching getAgentTeamSummary.
An entry after the window end is excluded.

A dispatch-time outreach withhold is anchored on COALESCE(agent_runs.started_at, solicitation_outreach.updated_at). rendered_at predates the refusal; updated_at is a general mutation timestamp a later write can move. commitWithhold sets agent_run_id in the same statement (dispatch.ts:1371-1379) and agent_runs.started_at (071:25) is DEFAULT NOW() with no updater, so the run start is the durable refusal time. updated_at is the fallback only for the best-effort path that leaves agent_run_id NULL.
A later mutation to a withheld outreach row does not move its entry between windows.
One account_audit_log suspension row yields exactly one entry in aggregate scope and exactly one in location scope — never one per location.
An impersonated admin session reads the impersonated account only, like every other dashboard read.
A past_due or cancelled subscription takes the existing SubscriptionUnavailableCard branch.
A location the caller does not own returns the uniform not-found response via resolveDashboardLocation.
An unrecognised source code reaching the read is a fault, not a category — assert rather than fall back to a default category.

rollback_plan: Not DB-touching. Revert the PR. No migration, no flag, no data written.
observability: The route logs under errorContext 'api/dashboard/refusals' through withDashboardOwnerRead, so a failed read raises the same Sentry signal as every other dashboard sub-route.
A source code with no mapping is a compile error for the four TypeScript enums and a test failure for the migration-111 outreach vocabulary. There is no runtime fallback to detect.
No new metric. If the tab renders and the category counts are non-zero for an account with a known held draft, it works.
